subject.title: Skipped group messages behind requireMention do not reach message hooks, which blocks full-history archive plugins

question: Should trusted installed plugins be allowed to observe mention-skipped inbound group messages through a public read-only hook, and does that hook require an explicit operator or plugin opt-in gate?
rationale: The requested hook enables the plugin use case, but it deliberately exposes content that current public plugin hooks do not see because mention gating prevents dispatch/session entry.

options.title: Approve a gated public hook
options.body: Add or require an explicit opt-in/access gate for `inbound_observed` so archive plugins can observe skipped messages only when the operator has enabled that visibility.

options.title: Approve installed-plugin trust as sufficient
options.body: Land the public read-only hook without an additional gate and document that installed plugins may observe skipped inbound content.

options.title: Keep only internal ingest for now
options.body: Decline the public hook until a broader plugin permission model or multi-channel design is ready.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated public hook
recommendation.body: Add or require an explicit opt-in/access gate for `inbound_observed` so archive plugins can observe skipped messages only when the operator has enabled that visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the shipped partial internal-hook implementation and are closest in history to the current skipped-message visibility boundary.
